note: Conversion batch #3 for the 45 BLOCKED_NEEDS_JULIA_SURFACE rows in docs/dev-log/core070/required-source-case-map.json whose function name (after stripping the POSTFIT-SURFACE- prefix and any S3 dot-suffix) matches an entry in names(GLLVM) as of this worktree's HEAD. Design discipline: EVERY R-side signature/return shape below was read directly from .unlazy/core070-aghq/oracle-source/readback/R/*.R -- never inferred from a Julia docstring -- per the wave-5/wave-6 lesson. That reading found that most of the 45 rows are SAME-NAME, DIFFERENT-SURFACE collisions (documented per-row in deferred[]): R's getREsd(fit, block=) covers auxiliary random-effect blocks Julia's getREsd(fit, y) does not touch at all (Julia's covers the latent factor scores R routes through getLV(se=TRUE) instead); R's compare_Sigma_table(x, truth, ...) compares a fit against a KNOWN GROUND-TRUTH matrix, not two fits; R's compare_dep_vs_two_psi(fit_two_psi, ...) is a phylogenetic 'two-psi' identifiability refit-and-compare specific to a named reparameterisation GLLVM.jl does not implement, not a generic two-fit bridge; R's vcov.gllvmTMB_multi returns the FULL (off-diagonal-capable) fixed-effect covariance block, Julia's vcov(fit,y) returns a Diagonal over ALL packed parameters; R's diagnostic_table(x, table=) requires x already carry gllvmTMB_diagnostic metadata attached by predictive_check()/residuals(), not a bare fit; R's profile_targets() is a READINESS REGISTRY (which parameters COULD be profiled, without running anything) while Julia's profile_targets() runs every target's curve directly. 7 source rows (6 distinct functions) survived that reading with a genuinely comparable R call shape on the reused gaussian_small fixture and are executable below; the remaining 38 are deferred with a per-row trace. Phylo-signal rows (profile_ci_phylo_signal, phylo_signal/profile_phylo_signal, profile_targets when phylo-scoped) are deferred per the task brief: no proven paired phylo fixture exists in this worktree's receipts (grep of test/parity/ and .unlazy/core070-aghq/ found no executed STRUCT-PHY paired fit), so inventing one is out of this lean batch's scope. slope_sd_ci is deferred for the same reason on the random-slope side: no healthy GaussianRandomSlopeFit fixture exists in this worktree's receipts, and R's own slope-sd-ci.R readback documents a prior hand-indexing failure mode on the phylo route.

cases.notes: Verified from check-auto-residual.R:60-141: on a fit with no per-row family mixing (fids all identical) and no ordinal-probit trait (family id 14), R returns invisible(list(status='ok', messages=character())) with no side-effect warning/error. gaussian_small is plain gaussian(), single family, no ordinal trait -> both sides must report the coherent/ok state.

Verified from methods-gllvmTMB.R:2017-2080: sanity_multi(object) returns invisibly a list with $converged (object$opt$convergence == 0) and $pd_hessian (sdreport pdHess flag) among other fields. gaussian_small is fit with control=gllvmTMBcontrol(n_init=1L, se=TRUE) so both should converge with a PD Hessian; compares converged==converged and pd_hessian truthy-vs-truthy (R's NA / Julia's missing both mean 'not applicable' and are treated as agreeing only when both sides report the same non-committal state).

Verified from rotate-loadings.R:428-447: R's compare_loadings(Lambda_a, Lambda_b) takes two RAW MATRICES and does a Procrustes rotation, returning $frobenius = ||Lambda_a_rot - Lambda_b||_F -- a genuinely different quantity/signature than Julia's compare_loadings(fit1, fit2) (which returns frobenius_norm_LLt, the rotation/sign-free ||Lambda1 Lambda1' - Lambda2 Lambda2'||_F tcrossprod invariant; ground rule: never compare signed Lambda entries). The two are not cross-comparable at any tolerance. What IS comparable without inventing a second model: each engine's own self-consistency when handed the SAME loadings matrix twice -- R's Procrustes frobenius(Lambda,Lambda) must be exactly 0 (perfect self-alignment), and Julia's frobenius_norm_LLt(fit,fit) must be exactly 0 (identical tcrossprod). This is an 'own_consistency' case (each side checked against its own zero, not against the other engine's number), mirroring the wave-6 own_receipt_defect pattern for a genuine surface-shape gap.

Verified from methods-gllvmTMB.R:2837-2839: fitted.gllvmTMB_multi(object, type='response') is a thin wrapper: predict(object, newdata=NULL, type='response'). Verified predict.gllvmTMB_multi (methods-gllvmTMB.R:2421-2483, in-sample newdata=NULL, default re_form=~. i.e. re_zero=FALSE) returns a data.frame(unit, species, trait, est=eta) in object$data's OWN row order -- eta = object$report$eta, the full conditional predictor including the latent-variable contribution. gaussian_small's df_g row order is site-major/trait-minor (site=rep(seq_len(n),each=p), trait=rep(trait_names,times=n)), which is exactly the column-major flatten of a p x n matrix -- so fit$est (a length p*n vector) lines up element-for-element with vec(eta_julia) where eta_julia is Julia's p x n predict() output (also column-major, also using the UNROTATED conditional latent score consistent with the model's own Lambda parameterisation, not an SVD-rotated basis). Gaussian identity link: type='response' == type='link', so no back-transform is needed on either side. This resolves the wave6-conversion1 blocker ('list object cannot be coerced' under as.numeric()) by reading the $est column instead of coercing the whole data.frame.

Same underlying quantity and row-order argument as CORE070-WAVE7-FITTED-MULTI (fitted() is a thin wrapper over predict() in R); kept as a separate case because it exercises the Julia predict() call path directly (src/postfit.jl:258-270) rather than through StatsAPI.fitted's forwarding method, and pays a distinct source_id (postfit/POSTFIT-SURFACE-predict.gllvmTMB_multi is a separate ledger row from fitted.gllvmTMB_multi).

Verified from predictive-diagnostics.R:229-260, AND by a live local (non-frozen) gllvmTMB dry run in this worktree: residuals.gllvmTMB_multi(object, type='randomized_quantile', scale='normal') (both R defaults) returns a 400-ROW DATA.FRAME (.row, trait, ..., residual, status, scale, method, seed), not a bare vector -- length(rs) on a data.frame returns its COLUMN count (15), not nrow (400), a trap the first reading of this function missed. The live dry run confirmed rs$residual == (df_g$value - fitted(fit_g)$est) / sigma_eps EXACTLY (cor==1, constant ratio == 1/sigma_eps across all 400 rows) -- the EXACT (non-simulated) per-family CDF quantile-residual route reduces to the standardized residual for the continuous Gaussian family, with no added randomization, confirmed numerically rather than assumed from the docstring. Julia's residuals(fit::GllvmFit, y; type=:dunnsmyth) docstring (src/postfit.jl:308-314) states the identical mathematical reduction. Row order: same p x n column-major convention as the FITTED-MULTI/PREDICT-MULTI cases above (rs$.row runs 1..400 in object$data's row order, matching vec() of Julia's p x n output).

NEW FINDING (verified from profile-targets.R against src/confint_profile.jl's own docstring): R's profile_targets() is a READINESS REGISTRY -- which parameters/targets COULD be profiled, without running anything, because TMB::tmbprofile() needs the fit's live tmb_obj checkpoint machinery to run cheaply and reversibly. NEW FINDING: R's predictive_check() and Julia's predictive_check(fit,y) are both genuine simulate-and-summarise checks with the same conceptual shape, but their RNG streams are not coupled across languages (R's stats::simulate() vs Julia's simulate(fit,n;rng)) -- only a STRUCTURAL comparison (matching (stat,trait) grid, p-values in [0,1] on both sides, no crash) is possible, never a numeric-tolerance comparison. Designing and validating that structural pass criterion (what counts as 'agreeing' between two independently-seeded Monte Carlo runs) needs its own design pass and is out of this lean batch's scope; the per-quantity comparison design in this contract is 'point' or 'verdict' only, neither of which fits an unpaired stochastic table.
Same RNG-decoupling issue as postfit/POSTFIT-SURFACE-predictive_check (duplicate ledger row).

NEW FINDING: gllvmTMB_check_consistency(fit,y) is a Monte-Carlo (n_sim re-simulations) score-centring diagnostic on both sides (R via TMB::checkConsistency(), Julia via a Hotelling T2 test on re-simulated packed-NLL scores per src/diagnostics.jl:24-133's own docstring), with independently-seeded RNGs in the two languages -- only a structural comparison (marginal_p_value in [0,1], no crash) is possible, and Julia's own docstring already documents this port does NOT reproduce TMB's internal joint/marginal Laplace split (re-simulates the generative model directly instead). Designing a defensible structural pass criterion is out of this lean batch's scope.

NEW FINDING, verified from diagnose.R:2005-2213 (gllvmTMB_diagnose returns invisibly a list with components sanity/rotation/Sigma_B/Sigma_W/ICC_site/communality_B/communality_W/hints -- no single pass boolean) and Julia's gllvmTMB_diagnose (src/diagnostics.jl:281-324, returns (pass, sanity, boundary_flags, messages)): R's return shape is a rich human-report list keyed by biological summaries (ICC, communality per tier), not a boolean-plus-flags verdict; Julia's is a boolean pass over a generic variance/correlation boundary scan documented in its own docstring as NOT covering R's per-family boundary rows (binomial-prevalence, multinomial degeneracy, ordinal cutpoint span, spatial-domain diameter). A defensible coarse verdict bridge (e.g. R's $hints being empty vs Julia's pass=true) is plausible but was not attempted here given the remaining scope in this batch; left for a follow-up wave with a dedicated comparison-design pass rather than guessed at under time pressure.
Same rich-report-vs-boolean-verdict shape gap as namespace/export/gllvmTMB_diagnose (duplicate ledger row).

NEW FINDING, verified from diagnose.R:1548-1958: R's check_gllvmTMB() returns a data.frame TABLE of named checks (optimizer_convergence, max_gradient, sdreport, ...) each with a PASS/WARN/FAIL/INFO status column and ~19 configurable thresholds, not a single pass boolean; Julia's check_gllvmTMB (src/diagnostics.jl:344-351) aggregates sanity_multi + check_auto_residual + the gllvmTMB_diagnose boundary scan into one pass::Bool. A coarse bridge (no FAIL row in R's table vs Julia pass=true) is plausible but needs the same dedicated comparison-design pass noted on gllvmTMB_diagnose above; deferred rather than guessed at under time pressure.

NEW FINDING, verified from diagnostic-tables.R:53-151: R's diagnostic_table(x, table=...) requires x to ALREADY carry gllvmTMB_diagnostic metadata (attr(x,'gllvmTMB_diagnostic')), attached by a prior call to predictive_check() or residuals() -- calling it on a bare gllvmTMB_multi fit aborts with 'x does not carry gllvmTMB diagnostic metadata'. Julia's diagnostic_table(fit; ...) (src/diagnostics.jl:372-405) instead takes the raw fit directly and computes everything itself. A genuine call-shape mismatch requiring an extra R-side pre-step (predictive_check(fit_g, Y_g) or residuals(fit_g) first) that was not designed and verified in this batch; deferred rather than guessed at.

NEW FINDING, verified from extract-sigma-table.R:494-544: R's compare_Sigma_table(x, truth, ...) compares a fit's implied Sigma table against a supplied GROUND-TRUTH matrix (typically the simulation's true covariance), not two fits against each other. Julia's compare_Sigma_table(fit1, fit2) (src/diagnostics.jl:487-512) is a two-fit bridge -- a genuinely different signature and purpose. gaussian_small's simulation truth (Lambda_true, sigma_true from tools/core070_surface_conversion_batch.R) COULD in principle be threaded through as R's `truth` argument, but that requires re-deriving R's `entries`/`measure`/`part` table-row semantics from extract_Sigma_table() to know which rows to compare against Julia's dense Sigma_y -- out of this batch's remaining scope; deferred.

NEW FINDING, verified from extract-two-psi-cross-check.R:488-556: R's compare_dep_vs_two_psi(fit_two_psi, threshold, phylo_vcv, phylo_tree) takes a SINGLE fitted phylogenetic 'two-psi' model and internally REFITS an alternative 'dep' model via .refit_alt(), comparing Sigma_phy/Sigma_non components -- a phylo-specific identifiability cross-check for a named reparameterisation GLLVM.jl does not implement as a distinct family. Julia's compare_dep_vs_two_psi(fit_dep, fit_alt, n) (src/diagnostics.jl:546-578) is explicitly documented as the generic two-fit bridge this gap forces, per its own docstring's 'Gap vs R' note. Not pairable without a phylo two-psi fixture, which per the task brief's phylo instruction does not exist in this worktree's receipts.
Same phylo-specific two-psi refit-and-compare mismatch as postfit/POSTFIT-SURFACE-compare_dep_vs_two_psi (extract-two-psi-cross-check.R:616-, the indep counterpart of the same construction).

R's confint_inspect() (confint-inspect.R:128-388) and Julia's confint_inspect(fit,y) (src/diagnostics.jl:667-711) are genuinely comparable in shape (both compare Wald vs profile-likelihood bounds per term and flag disagreement), but a live paired run needs per-term profile-likelihood CIs on BOTH engines for every packed term (~16 terms on gaussian_small: 5 trait coefficients + Lambda entries + sigma_eps), each requiring TMB::tmbprofile()-style bracket-then-bisect constrained refits on the R side and GLLVM.jl's own bracket-then-bisect profile_ci on the Julia side. That per-term profile-CI runtime budget is beyond what this lean batch attempted to verify feasible; deferred to a follow-up wave with a dedicated runtime budget rather than risking an unverified multi-minute R-side profile loop.

Julia's diagnose_kernel_separability(fit) (src/diagnostics.jl:449-461) only has a comparable non-trivial answer for a fit with a K_W (within/unit_obs) loading tier (Lambda_B vs Lambda_W); gaussian_small (K_W=0, single-tier) returns separable=missing by construction ('nothing to separate'). R's kernel-helpers.R/kernel-keywords.R separability check is scoped to kernel_* structured terms (a different structured-covariance mechanism than the K_W tier), so no fixture reused by this batch exercises a genuinely comparable non-trivial case on either side.

NEW FINDING: R's bootstrap_Sigma() (bootstrap-sigma.R) and Julia's bootstrap_Sigma(fit; level=:unit, n_boot=500, ...) (src/confint_derived_wald.jl:801-830) are genuinely comparable in shape (per-entry Sigma bootstrap percentile CIs), but the comparison is inherently STRUCTURAL, not exact-numeric (independent bootstrap draws in each language, per the task brief's 'bootstrap cases structural-only' guidance), AND the point estimate itself needs R's bootstrap_Sigma()'s exact reconstruct-formula machinery (.reconstruct_gllvmTMB_formula, referenced at the top of bootstrap-sigma.R) read and verified before a paired point-estimate case can be built safely. That verification pass was not completed within this batch's remaining scope; deferred rather than guessed at.

Julia's tmbprofile_wrapper(fit,param_index) (src/confint_profile.jl:643-690) forwards its lower/upper bounds from the already-tested profile_ci kernel, so a numeric pairing against R's confint(fit_g,parm='sigma_eps') (the exact quantity wave6's confint_sigma_eps_bounds case already proved pairable at 5e-3, see docs/dev-log/core070/wave6-conversion-batch-contract.json) is plausible in principle. It was not built here because R's TMB::tmbprofile()-backed tmbprofile_wrapper() is a genuinely different code path from confint()'s Wald route (checkpoint-based profile-curve machinery, not a Wald delta-method bound), and asserting the two converge to the same 5e-3-tolerance interval needs that TMB profile path exercised live, which this batch's remaining scope did not budget for; deferred to a follow-up wave with tmbprofile_wrapper's OWN R call, not confint()'s.
Same TMB-profile-vs-Wald-route verification gap as postfit/POSTFIT-SURFACE-tmbprofile_wrapper (duplicate ledger row).

R's simulate.gllvmTMB_multi() (methods-gllvmTMB.R:1431-) and Julia's simulate(fit::GllvmFit,n;rng) (src/families/aghq_gaussian_fit.jl:171) both draw parametric replicates from the fitted model, but their RNG streams are not coupled across languages -- only a structural comparison (matching shape, finite values, same marginal moments up to Monte Carlo error) is possible, and designing that structural pass criterion was not completed within this batch; same class of gap as predictive_check above.

NEW FINDING, verified from vcov-coef.R:69-98: R's vcov.gllvmTMB_multi(object) returns the FULL (potentially off-diagonal) covariance block of the FIXED-EFFECT (X_fix) coefficients only, read from sd_report$cov.fixed's 'b_fix' rows. Julia's vcov(fit,y) (src/postfit.jl:679-693) instead returns a Diagonal() over confint(fit,y)'s FULL packed-parameter set (fixed effects, loadings, sigma_eps, ...), with zero off-diagonal entries BY CONSTRUCTION. A partial diagonal-only comparison restricted to the trait-fixed-effect entries is conceivable (ignoring R's off-diagonal terms) but was not attempted here -- risks silently declaring victory on a genuinely different-scope quantity; deferred with this trace instead.

rejection_cases.expect: R refuses a non-fit argument; Julia's port does NOT validate its `fit` argument's type the way R's inherits() guard does (documented asymmetry, not a matching-refusal case)
rejection_cases.notes: R: check-auto-residual.R:62-64 cli_abort()s unless inherits(fit,'gllvmTMB_multi'). Julia: GLLVM.check_auto_residual(42) hits hasfield(typeof(42), :link) === false and hasfield(typeof(42), :C) === false (src/diagnostics.jl:161), so it falls through with mixed_family=false, ordinal_probit=false and returns coherent=true WITHOUT erroring. This is a genuine ASYMMETRIC-behavior finding (Julia's check_auto_residual has no type guard analogous to R's inherits() check) recorded here per-side rather than forced into a false 'both refuse' claim; expect_r_raised=true, expect_julia_raised=false is the CORRECT (verified) outcome, not a defect masked as a pass.

A case whose kind is not one of point/verdict/own_consistency must be rejected before the tape.
